3090320.findings: Three figures, a decal plate and three boxes. Two boxes carry a Treasury of Childhood oval logo (a tiny arched word above it is illegible), so the figures are a Treasury of Childhood range; Coalport is not confirmed and no Coalport backstamp or base mark is visible in any photo. Figures look like painted cold cast resin or polyresin, not bone china: seated girl in lace dress and blue bonnet with roses, drummer boy with toy soldier on a chequerboard base, girl in a bunny suit holding a baby. The plate has a transfer print of a girl in a bonnet (Lawrence Pinkie style image) with printed lines Lawrence, Mulder & Zoon and Amsterdam-Holland, which is the print publisher line and not a pottery mark; turquoise rope border with gilt scalloped edge; potter not identified.
3090320.condition: Figures and plate look undamaged in the photos; third box is a lilac lace trimmed box. Plate is on a clear plastic stand.
3090320.reason: Resin figures and a decal plate, no Coalport mark visible, low value.
3090320.marks_read: Plate: Lawrence, Mulder & Zoon, Amsterdam-Holland (print publisher line); boxes: Treasury of Childhood logo; no Coalport mark seen.

3090324.findings: Two groups. (1) Blue and white transfer printed set with gilt edges and a neoclassical swag, rosette and scroll border: one large plate or cake plate, a stack of plates and saucers, and several fluted cups, roughly 12 to 15 pieces. The base of a fluted cup (photo 2) shows a printed blue Portland vase device above the word WEDGWOOD. No ENGLAND, date code, registration mark or pattern name is legible, so the Wedgwood attribution is supported but the date is not confirmed (a printed vase mark with no ENGLAND can point to before 1891, but other marks may not be visible, so treat as late Victorian to early 1900s, unconfirmed). (2) Imari palette chinoiserie willow style group in orange, underglaze blue, green and gilt: one plate of about 8 to 9 inches and about three or four trios of coffee cans or cups with ring handles, saucers and plates, roughly 8 to 10 pieces. No maker's marks visible on these and they do not look lustre decorated as the title says; maker not identified.
3090324.condition: Ring of small brown spots and some staining around the fluted cup base; gilding mostly intact but worn on some edges; possible chip or flake to the rim of one blue plate (top right of photo 2); cups otherwise look sound. Not every piece is seen from every angle.
3090324.reason: Printed Portland vase WEDGWOOD mark on a late Victorian style blue and white set plus an Imari style group, modest but real value.
3090324.marks_read: Printed blue Portland vase device above WEDGWOOD on a fluted cup base; no ENGLAND, date code or pattern name legible; Imari style pieces show no marks.
